column1: # The gate's wall clock, one row per CI job: what each job costs, and the most it may cost.
# Five tab-separated columns. `seconds` and `floor` are the reference the verify job's advisory
# report compares a median of main runs against; `budget` is the ceiling a single run of the job is
# held to, and the run that breaks it is red; `measured` is that row's population -- the runs its
# own figures were taken over, as `<runs>@<date of the newest>`. `-` is a column that does not apply
# to the row, never a zero.
# Updated by hand, never by the workflow. A report that recomputed its reference from its own
# recent past would let a slowdown become the new normal one window at a time, and the accumulated
# growth would never appear in any single report.
# Seconds: the median first-step-to-last-step span over the completed main push runs the row's own
# stamp counts, which is the one place the population is written.
# Floor: how far a 12-run median moves at p95, in percent of the reference beside it rather than in
# seconds -- that same population reshuffled and re-cut into two windows of twelve, rounded up to a
# whole percent, and whole runs resampled rather than single jobs, because a slow runner slows every
# job on it. A job with no row here is reported as unreferenced rather than measured. p95 rather
# than p90 because a report holding no verdict is worth only what it is worth reading, and a floor
# speaking on half of the quiet pushes spends exactly that.
# Budget: the highest single-run span in the stamped population, plus a quarter of it or ten
# seconds, whichever is more, rounded up to the next five. A single run swings far wider than a
# median does -- `db` reached twice its median inside its stamped runs, `ops` 1.9 times --
# so a ceiling that never cries wolf on a quiet runner sits well above the reference, and a run
# over it is a re-run or a regression, in that order. Raising one costs the runs that justify it: a
# budget or a reference that rises against main carries a new stamp, refused otherwise by
# `scripts/checks/check_gate_budget.py` in the pull request's `commits` job. Lowering one is free.
# A check joining the gate records its measured cost here, the **gate** clause in
# `.claude/rules/ops.md` being what asks for it. A cost that sits inside its job's floor moves
# neither the reference nor the budget and takes no stamp of its own.
# `images` is measured and not budgeted: its span is the layer cache's before it is the tree's, and
# inside one stamped population its widest run costs seven times its narrowest, so the number a
# ceiling would be set from says more about which layers were warm than about the tree. The
# Dockerfile change most worth catching is the one that empties that cache, and the median report
# is its only guard.
# `commits` runs on pull requests alone, so its population is pull-request runs and its reference
# columns are `-`: the report is cut from main runs, where it never appears. `format` runs on every
# push to main and wherever a pull request's paths reach it, but its row is still cut from the
# pull-request runs its stamp counts, so its reference columns stay `-` until main runs exist to cut
# them from. Both stamps move on their own runs and never with the rows above them.
# `ops` answers to a shorter population than every other row cut from main runs, counted in its own
# stamp -- `commits` and `format`, carved out just above, are shorter still and are pull-request
# runs. `nginx/edge_test.sh` joined that scope partway through those rows' window, and a run
# from before that merge measures a gate this one is not. A population that short cannot be cut
# into two windows of twelve, so its floor is the p95 movement between two 12-run medians drawn
# with replacement from it. On the three rows computable both ways that draw lands within a point
# of the reshuffle -- once narrower -- and on `images` about half again as wide, so it is the
# method a short population leaves rather than a systematically looser one.
# `db`'s floor is wide because its window straddles the database tier's move to PyMongo and
# its distribution over workers: a reshuffle drawing runs from both sides of that merge moves the
# median about as far as the merge itself did. It narrows once the window clears the merge, and
# until then only a large change reaches the report on that row.
# `docs` gained two checks: `cell-prose` costs 0.05 s and `echo` 1.01 s over the whole corpus,
# measured locally on 2026-09-02 with the file listing already warmed, so the figures are the
# checks' own rather than the walk's. Their 1.06 s sits inside the floor the `docs` row carries.
# `docs` gained a third check: `scheme-token` costs 0.034-0.057 s over nine interleaved rounds with
# the file listing warmed, measured locally on 2026-09-05 on a sixteen-core machine carrying
# fourteen agent sessions, an editor and a browser, so the upper end reads that contention as much
# as the check. The second
# method resolves nothing and says so: the delta between a whole run carrying the check and one
# without falls inside that run's own 0.2 s spread, which is what a check this small looks like
# against a job this size. It sits inside the floor the `docs` row carries, and the ceiling it
# answers to is that row's budget, the total row carrying none behind it.
# `backend` gained a check: `check_test_estate.py` costs 1.90-1.96 s over six interleaved runs, each
# returning exit 0, measured locally on 2026-09-03 on a sixteen-core machine carrying ten other
# workloads, so both ends are upper bounds reading that contention as much as the check. It is
# pooled with the scope's other units, so the job pays that span only where the pool cannot start
# them all at once, and either way it sits inside the floor the `backend` row carries.
# `docs` gained five checks -- `diagram`, `error-codes`, `invariant-number`, `output-verbs` and
# `wrapped-path` -- and widened two populations, the module-header scope to every file the hash
# reader answers for and the prose corpus by the notice file, with the fork-pool read behind the
# comment ceiling and the fork's standard behind the rule families. Measured whole rather than per
# check: the docs checker over the fork's tree and the branch's tree, interleaved, five rounds after
# one warm run each, on 2026-09-07 with nothing else running -- 7988 ms at the fork's median against
# 9267 ms at the branch's, spreads 16 ms and 59 ms, a difference of 1.3 s. That sits inside the
# floor the `docs` row carries; the figures are one machine's upper bound, and the runner's own
# median is what the report compares.
# `docs` gained a check: `check_public_routes.py` costs 110-129 ms end to end, of which 73 ms is the
# check rather than this interpreter's own start, over seven interleaved rounds after one warm run,
# each returning exit 0. Measured locally on 2026-09-07 on a sixteen-core machine carrying a fleet
# of concurrent agent sessions, so both ends are upper bounds reading that contention as much as
# the check. It is pooled with the docs scope's other units, so the job pays that span only where
# the pool cannot start them all at once, and either way it sits inside the floor the docs row
# carries, so neither reference nor budget moves and neither takes a new stamp.
# `db` gained a guard in front of the tier: a claim that refuses a second gate run rather
# than letting it run beside the first. Measured locally on 2026-09-07 over five interleaved rounds
# of two hundred iterations, on a Windows machine carrying a dozen agent sessions -- 22.6-26.5 ms to
# take the claim and 22.8-27.5 ms to give it back, both ends reading that machine's process spawn as
# much as the guard, and each paid once per run. Their 0.05 s is a thousandth of the row's 49 s
# reference, against a floor of 40 percent of it, so neither the reference nor the 125 s budget
# moves and neither takes a new stamp. The figure is a development machine's, which is what the
# guard's own cost can be measured on: it runs before the tier rather than in it.
# `scripts`' binding unit measured three ways on 2026-09-07 on the sixteen-core machine: alone and
# idle, `selfcheck.sh` took 45.2-45.9 s over five runs; inside one full-form run it took 97 s beside
# the section's pytest, ruff and pyright; under a process spinning every core it took 236 s. The
# gap between alone and in-run is contention, the unit waiting on the machine rather than working,
# so the row's reference is the run's figure and not the unit's, and what would pay is reducing
# what the run competes for rather than splitting the unit or removing work from it. The section
# itself binds the run at 122 s, its pytest unit the last to close; no figure here moves a row.
# `scripts`' pytest unit was one module long: `--dist loadfile` hands a module whole to one worker,
# and `scripts/tests/test_check_docs.py` carried 118.6 s of a 121.8 s run at eight workers against
# about 65 s of work a worker, while the case loop beside it, one test of 69 s, was dispatched last
# because xdist orders `loadfile` scopes by how many tests each holds. The net now stands in five
# modules, `scripts/tests/test_check_docs*.py`, and its cases one test apiece. Measured on
# 2026-09-22 on the sixteen-core machine at 100 per cent CPU from a fleet of agent sessions, three
# interleaved rounds of the whole suite in two mirrors of one tree, every run exit 0: the load moved
# each run's summed item time from 2378 to 3820 s, so the raw walls overlap; simulated on each
# new-layout run's own item times, which the simulation reproduces within 7 per cent, the old layout
# costs 649, 534 and 783 s against 466, 399 and 666 s. Read again on 2026-09-23 on the idle
# machine, two interleaved pairs of the whole suite at eight workers after one warm run of each: 93.0
# and 89.7 s on the old layout (729 cases) against 67.0 and 67.2 s on the new (773 cases, one of
# them failing on a job the file then had no row for), so the worst run after the split beats the
# best before it. No figure here moves a row.
# `docs` gained a check: `check_log_quoting_class.py` costs 97-141 ms end to end, of which about
# 60 ms is the comparison rather than this interpreter's own start, over two spreads of ten
# interleaved rounds after one warm run, each returning exit 0. Measured locally on 2026-09-07 on a
# sixteen-core machine carrying a fleet of concurrent agent sessions, so both ends are upper
# bounds reading that contention as much as the check. It opens two files and expands two
# character classes, so its span follows neither the size of the tree nor that of the branch. It is
# pooled with the docs scope's other units, so the job pays that span only where the pool cannot
# start them all at once, and either way it sits inside the floor the docs row carries, so neither
# reference nor budget moves and neither takes a new stamp.
# `docs` gained a check: `section-reference` costs 95-103 ms over the whole corpus of 1045 files,
# the upper end taken with the page cache cleared beside the check's own, over nine rounds
# interleaved with `wrapped-path`, which read 12 ms against the same corpus. Measured locally on
# 2026-09-07 on a sixteen-core machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so both ends are upper
# bounds reading that contention as much as the check, and the pages it resolves against are read
# once a run by the checks beside it either way. The same run widened the prose corpus by this file,
# 74 documents to 75. It sits inside the floor the `docs` row carries, so neither the reference nor
# the budget moves and neither takes a new stamp.
# `scripts` gained six cases: `scripts/tests/test_scope_decisions.py` derives what each package
# reads of the other and holds `scripts/gate/scope_map.sh`'s cross-boundary arms to it. They cost
# 1.1 s at the median of six interleaved rounds of the module, 15.26-15.91 s carrying them against
# 14.46-15.37 s without, measured locally on 2026-09-09 on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying
# six agent sessions on one tree, so both ends read that contention as much as the cases. The module
# is one chunk under `--dist loadfile` and its unit is pooled with the section's other three, so the
# job pays that span only where the pool cannot start all four at once; either way it sits inside the
# floor the `scripts` row carries, so neither the reference nor the budget moves and neither takes a
# new stamp.
# `scripts` gained seven cases: `scripts/tests/test_unit_shards.py` drives the gate's two shard
# refusals beside two cases reading the shard matrix, `scripts/tests/test_regex_lead.py` lexes the
# regex-literal lead, and `scripts/tests/test_scope_decisions.py` derives what the frontend's db tier
# loads directly. Their calls cost 1.3-1.5 s together over three runs, the two refusal cases 1.0 s of
# it and the db-tier case 0.29-0.40 s, measured locally on 2026-09-23 on a sixteen-core Windows
# machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so both ends read that contention as much as the
# cases. The shard module is one chunk under `--dist loadfile` and the other two ride modules
# already dispatched, so the job pays that span only where the pool cannot start them beside the
# longest chunk; either way it sits inside the floor the `scripts` row carries, so neither the
# reference nor the budget moves and neither takes a new stamp.
# `frontend` gained forty test files rendering the editors through HeroUI on jsdom, and its row is
# cut from the five completed main push runs since they landed, 2026-09-19 to 2026-09-20: 243, 260,
# 264, 268 and 287 s first step to last, so the reference is their median and the budget the rule
# above over the widest. The floor keeps the figure the 24-run population gave it: five runs are too
# few to draw a twelve-run median from, and drawn with replacement they answer 5 percent, which
# reads the smallness of the population rather than the job. It is re-cut, floor included, once
# twelve such runs exist. The unit tests are the whole
# move, 171 s on the runner against 35 s in the last stamped window, and the cost is each file's own
# process loading jsdom (1.05 s) and the HeroUI entry point (1.31 s) before a case runs, measured
# locally on 2026-09-19 on the sixteen-core machine: a file rendering nothing starts in 0.2 s and
# one rendering a rail in 2.9 s. Two levers were measured on that file over four interleaved rounds
# and rejected: Node's compile cache read slower than it saved, 3.8 s against 2.9 s, and dropping
# source maps altogether saves 0.25 s a file at the cost of every stack trace naming lines no file
# on disk holds. Both rejections stand: the compile cache re-measured on 2026-09-22 saved 4 percent
# of a rendering file's CPU with overlapping spreads, and the `test:base` script maps the application's
# frames still, dropping only `node_modules`' (`fl_frontend/app-source-maps.mjs`), whose frames no
# stack trace of ours reads.
# `fl_frontend/src/shared/testing/renderTest.ts` keeps each compiled component under
# `fl_frontend/node_modules/.cache/render-test`, keyed on its path and text, the harness and the
# installed TypeScript, and loads the compiler only on a miss. Over the whole unit suite, measured
# locally on 2026-09-23 on the sixteen-core Windows machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions:
# 515.9-528.2 s of summed CPU in four runs without it, 443.6-494.2 s in four starting from an empty
# cache, which is every CI run, and 425.4-460.7 s in four with it filled, the failing-case set
# identical in each interleaved round. Neither the reference nor the budget moves and neither takes
# a new stamp.
# `frontend-units` is one matrix job, and each of its instances is a row of its own under the name
# the job's `name:` template spells, which is the name the runs API reports and both the report and
# the budget check look a row up by. A row shared by the instances would have both readers fold
# names in step with each other, and the total would count one shard's span where every shard ran.
# Their four budgets are cut by the rule above from this branch's three pull request runs, the
# first that ran the shards; a reference and a floor need main's push runs, so both stay `-`.
# `scripts` gained two cases: `scripts/tests/test_check_gate_budget.py` holds the `verify` job's
# `needs` to every other job in the workflow, and drives that reader over a job left out of it. They
# cost 0.546-0.593 ms a pass together over nine interleaved rounds in two runs, each case called
# directly rather than through pytest. Measured locally on 2026-09-23 on a sixteen-core Windows
# machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so both ends are upper bounds; neither the reference
# nor the budget moves and neither takes a new stamp.
# `format` measured two ways of skipping the walk under `..`, which lists `fl_frontend/node_modules`
# and `.git` because prettier's own exclusions do not match there, and rejected both on their
# verdicts rather than their clocks. Prettier's fast CLI (`--experimental-cli`, prettier 3.9.6)
# checked the same files and passed a planted import-order swap the legacy CLI fails. Running the
# legacy CLI from the repository root, with `.prettierrc.json` naming its plugins by path, checked
# the same 1055 files and passed the same swap: prettier-plugin-tailwindcss runs the import sorter
# only when it can resolve that plugin by its package name, which it cannot from the root. Measured
# locally on 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-23 on a sixteen-core machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions.
# `db` gained the interleaved race cases and moved no figure. Two of them had parked a
# reopening at its first read of the referee, past its own write of the reopened fixture, so the
# erasure landing inside it waited out the transaction's sixty-second lifetime: 90 s and 73 s of a
# 185 s local run, and the runner's 208 s over this row's budget was the same wait. Parked at the
# reopening's first read of `spiele` the two take 0.08 s each, and the tier runs its 1113 cases in
# 21 s locally at width 6 on 2026-09-19, its slowest case 1.04 s.
# `docs` gained a rule: `check_tracked_text.py` refuses an invisible character beside a conflict
# marker, and that rule costs 60.9-62.1 ms over the corpus it already walks -- 1235 files read as
# text, 13.3 million characters -- against 686.7-705.6 ms for the conflict rule over the same corpus
# in the same process, the two arms interleaved across eight rounds. Measured locally on 2026-09-21
# on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions and an editor, so both ends
# are upper bounds reading that contention as much as the rule. The walk and the byte read are the
# checker's already, so that span is the whole marginal cost: one character-class scan answers a file
# holding none, which is nearly every file, and only a file with a hit is walked character by
# character. It sits far inside the floor the `docs` row carries, so neither the reference nor the
# budget moves and neither takes a new stamp.
# `frontend`'s unit tests were cut on 2026-09-22 by three changes to what each test file's process
# loads, measured as the summed CPU of every file's process on the sixteen-core Windows machine
# under a live fleet, over a frozen copy of HEAD, every run 292 files and 5131 passing cases:
# 834-896 s across five runs of the old `test` line against 518-533 s across two of the new one.
# Against the old line, the alias hook skipping TypeScript suffixes for a `node_modules`
# parent is about 5 percent, source maps for the application's modules alone about 6 percent, and a
# HeroUI or icon import loading only the names it takes, about 26 percent, a rendering file's
# process loading 2081 modules where it loaded 4160. Per-component subpath imports hold that now,
# loading the same modules within 40 in four of five sampled files; the fifth reaches
# `useOverlayState`'s root import. The runner's own figures replace these on the pull request's
# runs; no row moves until a population of them exists.
# `db` gained the frontend's db-tier files (`pnpm run test:db`, two files, each starting its
# own replica set through testcontainers) and the frontend toolchain step they need. The files cost
# 18.0-18.5 s over three runs measured locally on 2026-09-23 on a sixteen-core Windows machine
# carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so an upper bound; the install step was not measured. That is
# 37 % of the job's reference, inside its floor before the install is counted, so neither figure
# moves here: the first main runs carrying the step decide whether the row is re-stamped.
# `format`, `frontend`, the `frontend-units` shards and `db` gained a guard ahead of their
# scopes: `fl_frontend/node_modules` must exist, so a run without the install refuses rather than
# grading its absence. 58-60 microseconds a call over five interleaved rounds of two thousand calls
# against an empty loop, measured locally on 2026-09-23 on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying
# a fleet of agent sessions, so an upper bound; it is paid once in each gate process those scopes
# start. That is far inside every floor those rows carry, so no reference or budget moves and none
# takes a new stamp.
# `scripts` gained eleven cases and lost eleven. `scripts/tests/test_pre_commit.py` commits through
# `.githooks/pre-commit` in fresh repositories, two on `main` and one on a branch, 1.26-1.34 s for the
# three; `selfcheck.sh` step 12's registration read, with its script missing and present,
# 0.43-0.45 s; `scripts/tests/test_gate_forms.py`'s pool-fallback notice, one gate run no pool
# serves and one the scope pool serves, beside the list of pooling scopes, 2.20-2.28 s with the
# module's fixture built afresh on every call; `scripts/tests/test_scope_decisions.py`'s db-tier arm
# read against what the tier loads, 1.07-1.11 s on the module's fixture and 1.79 s where it builds
# it; the launcher the two test tiers share and the shard matrix's one axis and count, under a
# millisecond each. Measured locally on 2026-09-23 over five rounds in rotated order, each case
# called directly, on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so every
# figure is an upper bound. The eleven cut --
# step 12's watchdog comparison, the two shard-matrix readers above and `job_names`' two samples --
# started no gate run. Neither the reference nor the budget moves and neither takes a new stamp.
# `backend` gained a guard: `fl_backend/tests/tier.py :: TierGuard` watches every default-tier test
# through the driver's command listener, wrappers around each test's setup, call and teardown and
# around every fixture's setup, and a hook after each fixture's finalisation. The whole default tier
# took 49.8-55.6 s without it and 50.5-66.3 s with it, three interleaved rounds each in the gate's
# own serial form with `tests/core/test_tier.py` left out of both, the two quieter rounds putting
# the guard at 0.5-0.7 s. Measured locally on 2026-09-25 on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying
# a fleet of agent sessions, so both spreads are upper bounds. The guard's cost sits inside the
# floor the `backend` row carries; neither the reference nor the budget moves and neither takes a
# new stamp.
# `ops` traded three mirror checkers for one exposure check and a header block in the edge test.
# `nginx/edge_test.sh`, its header block now asking every location, took 3.21-3.33 s against
# 2.85-3.08 s for the redaction test alone, three interleaved rounds each, measured locally on
# 2026-09-23 on a sixteen-core machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so both ends are upper
# bounds. It sits inside the floor the `ops` row carries, and no row moves.
# `scripts` gained a module: `scripts/tests/test_pre_commit_format.py` commits through
# `.githooks/pre-commit` in fresh repositories, each case starting a real `node` through
# `.githooks/format-staged.mjs`. It took 44.5-115.0 s over five runs of the module alone against
# 8.3-16.8 s for its six cases before the hook formatted the stage in one node process,
# interleaved, and the three cases holding the hook's refusal of a commit its own formatting
# emptied took 4.3-13.0 s of it. Measured locally on 2026-09-25 on a sixteen-core Windows machine
# carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so every figure is an upper bound. `--dist loadfile` hands
# the module to one worker, where it is among the suite's longest chunks.
# `scripts` gained a module: `scripts/tests/test_deploy_edge_config.py` drives the deploy's edge
# functions behind a stand-in `docker`, 10.0-10.7 s over three runs of the module alone against
# 5.8-6.0 s for `scripts/tests/test_deploy_streams.py` interleaved with it, measured locally on
# 2026-09-25 on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so an upper
# bound. It is shorter than the pre-commit module above, so it sits inside the floor the `scripts`
# row carries and no row moves. `ops` runs `nginx -t` over `nginx/prod/` mounted by directory, as
# production mounts it; the edge test mounts each file of `nginx/local/` by name beside its stub.
# `ops` gained a second nginx in the edge test, serving `nginx/prod/` behind a certificate made for
# the run so the www redirect is requested, a render of the local stack's model so the edge starts
# as compose starts it, a drive of its Control API, and a stand-in upstream sending a copy of every
# security header. The edge test took 9.2-10.1 s over five runs against 3.7-6.5 s for the test
# before it, interleaved, and 9.2-10.1 s without the header copies in the same rounds, one run of
# 99.8 s under a saturated processor aside, so the copies cost less than this machine resolves.
# The scope also gained the two Compose renders, 459-494 ms each; `check_compose_model.py` over
# both, 155-164 ms end to end against 85-96 ms for the interpreter's own start, its connector-trust
# rule 0.21-0.24 ms a call against 0.88-0.99 ms for its other rules; and a `docker image inspect`
# ahead of `nginx -t`, 332-364 ms on a host holding the image, the pull it guards being the one the
# parse paid before. Measured locally on 2026-09-25 on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying a
# fleet of agent sessions, so every figure is an upper bound. The edge test's medians differ by
# 5.5 s, past the 4.9 s floor the `ops` row carries before the renders are counted, so the first
# main runs carrying them decide whether the row is re-stamped.
# `scripts` lost the comment classifier, its cases and its self-check step, and, when the local
# scope mapping went, the cases in `scripts/tests/test_scope_decisions.py` that listed a fixture
# branch or ran `verify.sh` over it. That module now takes 14.0-18.4 s against 29.2-71.4 s before
# the mapping went, and `scripts/tests/test_gate_pool.py`, whose order case holds one unit open for
# a second, 5.9-7.4 s against 4.9-10.4 s, three interleaved rounds each, measured locally on
# 2026-09-25 on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so upper bounds.
# The scope's cost falls; lowering one is free, and no row moves.
# `scripts` and `backend` gained a rule: ruff's `RUF100` refuses a `noqa` directive that suppresses
# nothing. `ruff check --no-cache` took 505-753 ms with it against 495-716 ms without over
# `scripts`, and 563-835 ms against 520-881 ms over the backend's `app` and `tests`, over eight
# interleaved rounds, each run exit 0, measured locally on 2026-09-24 on a sixteen-core Windows
# machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions. The arms overlap, so the rule costs less than this
# machine resolves. Neither the reference nor the budget moves and neither takes a new stamp.
# `frontend` gained a check: knip costs 1.97-5.50 s over six runs interleaved with tsc, which took
# 5.39-28.79 s in the same rounds, the widest its first and cold, measured locally on 2026-09-24 on
# a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so both ends are upper bounds.
# It is pooled with tsc, eslint and the audit and ran shorter than tsc in every round, so the job
# pays it only as contention; either way it sits inside the floor the `frontend` row carries, so
# neither the reference nor the budget moves and neither takes a new stamp.
# `backend` gained a check: deptry over `app/` (`scripts/gate/verify.sh :: do_backend_deps`) costs
# 328-2045 ms end to end, of which 340-462 ms at the median is deptry rather than this
# interpreter's own start, over two spreads of ten rounds interleaved with a bare interpreter after
# one warm run of each, every run returning exit 0. Measured locally on 2026-09-24 on a sixteen-core
# Windows machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so both ends are upper bounds reading that
# contention as much as the check. It is pooled with the scope's other units, so the job pays that
# span only where the pool cannot start them all at once, and either way it sits inside the floor
# the `backend` row carries, so neither the reference nor the budget moves and neither takes a new
# stamp.
# `images` gained two steps: each image's layer cache is exported to the Actions cache by a buildx
# run of its own after the probes, where the build carried the export before. On two pull-request
# runs on 2026-09-24 the two exports, run side by side, took 14 s and 8.5 s, then 13 s and 2.4 s,
# so the job pays the frontend's; the section took 117 s and 108 s, and the job 128 s and 114 s
# first step to last, against 155 s and 168 s on the same day's last run before the split, which
# built and exported in one step. Which layers each runner found warm is unknown, so the three spans say only that the
# split costs no more than the export already did. Its 13-14 s sits inside the floor the `images`
